messages:
Alex (AE): Hey team — FinBank wants to run a 1-week on-prem POC in an isolated datacenter. Main asks: fully offline installer, how we do license activation without internet, delta upgrades for the POC, and any blockers (OS/kernel, disk, network). Can we summarize needs + ops checklist? cc @Marta @Sam @Claudia

Marta (Solutions Eng): TL;DR: doable. Two delivery modes for POC: full offline bundle (OCI tar + manifests + runtime shim) or delta bundles (patch diffs). Recommend: start with full bundle to avoid first-time dependency issues, then switch to deltas for follow-ups.
- Full bundle size: ~6.8GB (includes images + default sample models).
- Typical delta bundle: <200MB (minor patch).
- Requirements we need from customer: container runtime (containerd or docker), kernel >= 5.4, systemd available, 80GB free disk for default install (less if they strip models), outbound blocked is fine — we don't need internet for install.
- Ops checklist to confirm before POC: VM/host OS image, disk layout, container runtime version, timezone & NTP, local artifact transfer method (USB / SCP), and a person with root access for install window.

Sam (Platform Eng): Implementation notes — artifacts are signed and shipped with a manifest.json (sha256 per file). For offline verify we instruct them to run:

```
echo "<sha256>  redwood-offline-v1.3.0.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
```
We also provide an `offline-activate` CLI that consumes a license JWT file we hand to them:
```
./offline-activate --license-file finbank-license.jwt --org finbank
```
The license file contains a nonce + expiry and is signed by our licensing service. For delta updates we produce a signed delta.tar and a manifest with layer diffs; they apply with `redwood-update apply delta-v1.3.1.tar` (no internet required).

Claudia (Security): A few security/gov items from Legal/Security:
- We require the standard security questionnaire filled (we can pre-fill most answers).
- Offline activation: we support a KMS/HSM-backed keywrap workflow where the license JWT is sealed by customer's HSM if they request. If they can't provide HSM, we recommend storing license.jwt in the OS keystore (instructions included).
- Attestation checklist: NTP enabled, minimal outbound connections, host integrity (sha256 for installers verified), and a signed manifest.
- We will need confirmation on their patch/vulnerability SLAs — if they expect weekly CVE fixes we need an enterprise SLA add-on.

Ravi (SRE): Upgrade cadence / operational constraints:
- Recommended: monthly security micro-patches (delta bundles) and quarterly minor releases.
- For enterprise with SLA we can commit to weekly hotfix bundles (paid).
- Upgrade window: expect 10–30 minutes for control-plane rolling upgrade; autoscaling workloads may take longer. We require a maintenance window for stateful components.
- Rollback path exists, but operators MUST snapshot /var/lib/redwood before upgrade. Rollback command (example):
```
redwoodctl snapshot create --path /backups/finbank-preupgrade
redwoodctl rollback --to v1.3.0
```
- Ports & network: air-gapped install needs allowed internal ports (gRPC between nodes), we will send a minimal port matrix. No outbound internet required.

Marta (Solutions Eng): A couple more practical notes:
- For smallest transfer payloads we can provide an OCI-layout tar (docker/ctr load compatible) or a pre-assembled VM image. If the customer wants incremental security patches, we provide delta bundles built as layer diffs so rsync/USB transfers are small.
- We sign everything with our release key; manifest includes release URL, sha256s, and GPG signature fingerprint. Example manifest verification snippet we give them:
```
# verify tar
sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
# verify signature
gpg --verify manifest.json.sig manifest.json
```
- Legal/licensing: offline license activation is allowed; activation tokens are single-use and bound to an org ID and expiry. We can extend expiry on request for POC.

release-bot: Release 1.3.0 (offline bundle) uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/releases/1.3.0/offline.tar.gz (signed). Manifest fingerprint: "ABCD:1234:EF56:...". Delta bundle for 1.3.1 (security micro-patch) available: s3://redwood-artifacts/deltas/1.3.1/delta.tar.gz

Alex (AE): This is great — I'll summarize for FinBank: full bundle for initial POC, delta path for follow-ups, need host image and root access during install window, security questionnaire + confirmation on HSM or keystore approach, and agree on upgrade cadence (monthly by default, weekly requires SLA). I'll book a call to lock OS image + maintenance windows. Thanks all :pray:
